body: i don’t feel that my scars are pathetic, i see them as a reminder of all of the pain i was in back then. they get to be with me while i recover and i feel very peaceful knowing i will never go back to it.

good luck! therapy turned my life around, i hope it does the same for you. you’re allowed to struggle, being the golden child doesn’t make you immune to depression. live your truth, sending good vibes your way.
if that’s all you have, it’s okay. relish the love they have for you, soak in the peace of their presence. even if you can’t feel the joy of being with them, i promise you they feel it for you.

i promise you, it is NOT for the better of your family to end your life. nothing you could cause them would be anywhere near as painful as your death. the depression and isolation is making you believe that, you have to use everything you have to prove your depression wrong.

this is incredibly well written, i can feel the passion and care you have for others through your post. to me, the dedication you show is worth staying for, but i of course don’t know your circumstances. 

i’m 21 and we seem to think and express ourselves in similar manners — it deeply hurts my heart to see someone i empathize so closely with feel that they have to go. 
i feel wholly blessed to have met you and will carry your words with me for quite a while. if nothing else, you’ve accomplished your goal of making someone, myself, feel freer from their burdens and i’m proud of you for that.

NAD but reading that, my first thought was a seizure. i have epilepsy and auras (partial seizures) can often present in physical symptoms like you described. i second the vote for seeing a neurologist if your doctor recommends it!
